blocks.text: EngineConfig = { networking?: { mode?: "singleplayer" | "multiplayer" // Networking mode. Default: "multiplayer": each player owns their own state, zero-correction movement, the server applies and fans out without simulating. "singleplayer" = nothing is shared. } ui?: { // Engine UI configuration theme?: { // UI theme settings applied to all game UI font?: string // Default font family for game UI. Any CSS font-family string works. Bundled fonts (always available): 'Geist Pixel Square', 'Geist Pixel Grid', 'Geist Pixel Circle', 'Geist Pixel Triangle', 'Geist Pixel Line', 'Jersey 10' (legacy). Geist Pixel Grid, Circle, Triangle and Line draw each pixel of a letter apart, so the background shows between them and small text looks striped or broken. You can also use any font name: it's applied as CSS so system fonts and web-safe fonts work too (e.g., 'Georgia', 'Courier New', 'Impact'). If the font isn't available, the browser falls back to system-ui, sans-serif. Set via `ctx.world.engine.ui.theme.font = 'Geist Pixel Square'`. } targetFps?: number // Game-UI (HUD) refresh rate in frames per second. Default 30, the default simulation rate: the HUD samples game state once a simulation frame at most, so a rate past the place's tick rate samples every frame and no more. For smoother motion, animate with CSS transitions/keyframes inside the HUD html: they run on the browser clock at full display refresh. Lower it (10, or 1 for once a second) to spend less on a mostly-static HUD. Set via `ctx.world.engine.ui.targetFps = 15`. Applies live: no reload. referenceHeight?: number // Opt-in HUD viewport normalization: the viewport HEIGHT (px) the game UI was designed against. Unset (the default), authored px land as-is: a HUD laid out on a 4K monitor covers twice the screen fraction on a 1080p one. Set, the engine scales the game-UI plane by `viewportHeight / referenceHeight` (CSS zoom, live on resize), so authored px mean "px at the reference height" and the HUD holds the same screen fraction on every monitor; the UI script's `window.innerWidth`/`window.innerHeight` mirror reports the same reference space (`innerHeight` reads exactly `referenceHeight`). Use the height the UI was designed on: 1080 for most, 2160 for a HUD laid out on a 4K screen, 180 for a 320 × 180 pixel-art HUD. Game HUD only: god-mode chrome is engine-owned and never scales. Set via `ctx.world.engine.ui.referenceHeight = 1080`. Applies live: no reload. } graphics?: { // Rendering configuration perfectPixelArt?: boolean | number // true draws a place seen through an orthographic camera, 2D or 3D, on its pixel art's own grid, read from its sprites and tiles; a number sets texels per world unit. Default false. A pixel look over any picture is the look's `pixelate` antialias?: boolean // Antialiasing. Smoothing is the player's own choice (`off`, or `msaa` at 4 samples); a world cannot turn it on. `false` forces raw pixels: one scene sample, no multisampling, even when the player chose `msaa`. It never holds the picture's size: in 3D the quality governor may render fewer pixels and upscale; a 2D scene never does. Applies live on patch. } playerSettings?: { // Creator policy over PLAYER settings: accessibility protections a game pre-enables for players who never chose, and which player control overrides are legal. A player's own explicit choice always wins within these bounds. Sound, Savi-verbosity and graphics quality have NO surface here by design: the game's mix is authored in spec audio objects, how chatty Savi is belongs to the player, and a game never sets or caps a player's quality level: each player's device is measured and the player chooses their own. Set each key at its dot (`ctx.world.engine.playerSettings.<path> = …`); `null` clears it. Illegal fields are refused with a warn naming why (e.g. accessibility may only be pre-enabled, never disabled: no creator can force flashing on a photosensitive player). defaults?: { // Starting values for settings the player never set explicitly: a player's explicit choice always beats these. accessibility?: { reduceFlashing?: boolean; reduceMotion?: boolean } // Safe direction only: `true` pre-enables a protection for this game; `false` is refused (players own accessibility). } caps?: { // Hard bounds: legal only for controls. Accessibility and graphics quality can never be capped. controls?: { lookSensitivity?: boolean; invertY?: boolean; fov?: boolean } // Which player control overrides are legal in this game (default: all overridable). Creator control VALUES live in spec.camera / spec.inputs. } } simulation?: { tickRateHz?: number } // The WORLD layer of the simulation tick base, `simulation.tickRateHz` (Hz): the default place's `tickBase` shadows it, and the room steps every place at that one rate; unset, the era default. The same chain `ctx.place.tickBase` names as the layer beneath it. behaviors?: ScriptRef[] // Engine behavior scripts, lifecycle hooks as named exports: onArrive(ctx, player) / onLeave(ctx, player) fire for every player arrival and departure at the WORLD's door (join, rejoin, a link in from another world: one hook each way; `player.arrival.kind` says which; see platform-systems) (a hop between places of one world runs the place's policy.onArrive / onLeave instead), plus onPlaceStart / onPlaceShutdown. Same composition pattern as entity behaviors. crons?: { schedule: string; script: ScriptRef }[] // Cron jobs: scheduled scripts. Each script exports `async function cron(objectApi)`. }
